purpose: Test the inventory profile's catalogue-scan hotspot while preserving every authored result and random draw
variant: An owner builds a lazy tag-to-row index, unions matching row ids and restores authored row order before applying exclusions; existing base and weighted caches stay owner-local
correctness: Existing SDK tests use the isolated candidate runtime, including all recorded item and mint-stream fixtures
All authored bases and synthetic open, explicit, empty-tag, duplicate-tag and exclusion combinations preserve ordered pool membership
Long seeded streams, restore, interleaved owners and different base affinities preserve items, modifiers and RNG/uid snapshots
Persistent native-library consumers retain their gameplay and ownership results with the candidate bundle

timing.primary: Existing 320-command inventory course at batch 64 with a fresh logical session per sample
controls: Steady item stream after pool warmup
First affix request in a fresh generator
timing.policy: All samples retained; both orders must pass; profiler samples are not acceptance timings

memory.policy: Compare equivalent warmed owners and state. This is an experiment guard, not a device-memory budget; zero tracked leaks remains required

decision: No production promotion until correctness, controls and memory guard pass. No milestone 43 threshold changes or hardware-support claims
